corrections: Qualified Snowflake-style IDs: uniqueness depends on node allocation, clock rollback handling and sequence bounds, while time-based IDs are not strictly globally ordered across nodes.
Separated unique message identity from conversation ordering and removed a fixed per-host WebSocket connection claim that depends on workload and operating-system limits.
Clarified that database persistence, acknowledgements and offline pull reduce loss windows but do not create unconditional end-to-end delivery guarantees.
Clarified that at-least-once delivery permits duplicates; idempotency keys only suppress duplicates within their consistency and retention boundary.
Replaced the claim that a database write and Kafka publish normally share a transaction with the transactional-outbox boundary and explicit idempotent consumption.
Changed fixed Feed fan-out thresholds into capacity-planning examples driven by follower activity, publish frequency, latency objectives and cost.
Qualified Redis Lua inventory deduction as atomic on one Redis execution context, not proof of cross-system order and stock consistency.
Reframed payment safety as ledger invariants, durable history, idempotency and reconciliation rather than an absolute no-overcharge/no-undercharge promise.
Corrected timing-wheel complexity: pointer advancement and insertion can be constant or amortized, while bucket scans, cascades, storage and execution are workload-dependent.
Removed constant-time FST lookup wording and fixed search latency/candidate-count claims; lookup and collection depend on term length, postings, cache state and query shape.
Reframed search suggestion, recommendation, CDN and live-streaming latency numbers as example SLO budgets that require workload-specific percentile measurement.
Qualified Kafka durability and ordering by acknowledgement, replication and partition boundaries, and HNSW performance by recall/latency configuration trade-offs.
Removed the implication that geographic proximity guarantees the lowest CDN latency or that synchronous multi-region replication alone proves RPO=0.
Reviewed the remaining system-design pages for failure boundaries, consistency scope and capacity assumptions; unchanged illustrative numbers are examples rather than universal platform guarantees.

relationSuggestions.reason: Chat messages need stable unique IDs, while strict conversation ordering requires a separate per-conversation sequencing boundary.
API gateways commonly enforce admission control, but distributed rate-limit consistency and failure policy remain explicit choices.
Flash-sale architectures use layered admission control before inventory mutation.
Notification routing composes channel-specific push delivery with retries, deduplication and preference policy.
Regional health, replication lag and SLO measurements are inputs to failover decisions.
Crawler output feeds parsing and indexing, while crawling and retrieval retain separate freshness and correctness boundaries.
Both use lexical indexes and ranking, but suggestion serves prefix candidates under different latency and freshness objectives.
